headline: The proposal's real architectural contribution is not its numbers or its pipeline — it is three seams we structurally lack: (1) rules as a **declarative, enumerable registry** with typed actions instead of imperative checks scattered across `methodRules`, `eqmDeviceMeetsRow`, `deviceCanReach`, `schedulePlacements` and a Phase-3a `safetyGate`; (2) **outcome→path routing** — the user states a result ("shreddable, crisp bark, sweet") and the engine *selects among already-cited paths*, which composes perfectly with our cited-only rule because routing picks, it never authors a number; (3) **conditional stage boundaries** (`TRIGGER_NEXT_STAGE_WHEN internal==71°C`), where we have none at all — our `planSchedule` is pure fixed-duration backward chaining and the wrap point, the single most consequential event in a long cook, sits in a prose field (`mid:"עטיפה ב-70°C"`) that `itemStages` never reads. Our citation machine, occupancy model, negative-case engineering and hold-safety floors are genuinely better than theirs and must not be traded away. The correct integration is a **rules layer under `itemStages`, not beside it**: `itemStages` stays the single stage authority, rules become the thing that *feeds* it, and every rule emits a typed code + cited numeric params so the render layer keeps its `L(he,en)` monopoly and Guards A/B/C never see engine prose.

conceptsFound.concept: Master Recipe / parameter engine — one parameterized recipe generating many results instead of N independent recipe rows
conceptsFound.steelman: A recipe is not a row of numbers; it is a STRUCTURE (ordered stage kinds, trigger kinds, modifier slots) plus a small set of cited scalars. Most of what differs between 130 cuts is the scalars, not the structure. Hold structure once, per archetype; hold only cited deltas per cut. Implemented well, adding a new cut becomes 'pick archetype + supply 6 cited numbers', and a structural improvement (e.g. adding a wrap trigger) propagates to 90 recipes at once instead of 90 hand edits.
conceptsFound.value: We already proved this pattern works here: `equipment_map.py` derives an `equip` block for all 279 recipes from what the recipe already encodes, explicitly so it 'cannot drift out of sync'. The same derivation applied to process structure would collapse the repetition in `mid`/`somid`/`wrap`/`sear` and make structural fixes O(1) instead of O(279). Compression is the SECOND-order benefit; the first-order benefit is that a structure you can name is a structure a rule can attach to.

conceptsFound.concept: Outcome→path routing: user states desired result, engine translates to a process flow (§2.3, §3.2, §8's three route buttons)
conceptsFound.steelman: The user's mental model is the plate, not the appliance. Ask for texture/crust/smoke/speed; the engine RANKS the paths that produce it. Critically, in our world this never invents a number — it filters and orders `itemPaths(meta)`, all of which are already cited. The named path becomes the subtitle, not the headline.
conceptsFound.value: This is the single highest-value idea for us and it lands exactly where we are about to build. `itemPaths(meta)` returns engine labels ('⚡ סו-ויד + עישון'); the user must already know what that yields. `gearAwareDefault` routes by EQUIPMENT (and does so better than their §4.3), but nothing routes by RESULT. CP2 is 11 tasks from shipping a panel that lists paths by name — turning it outcome-first is the difference between a settings screen and a product.

conceptsFound.concept: Additional outcome axes with real effects: crispness, finish tenderness, glaze timing, sauce-at-serving — and chewiness as a PREDICTED output ('will this come out chewy?')
conceptsFound.steelman: Doneness is one axis of many. Crust, chew and juiciness are governed by different levers (surface dryness + finish heat; collagen dwell time; bath temp + evaporation) and can be surfaced as separate, cited-backed choices. Chewiness is the one that should be an OUTPUT, not an input: given the path the user picked, the engine predicts 'this will be chewy' and names the cited fix — which is a warning nobody in this category ships.
conceptsFound.value: We ship exactly one axis (`doneness`, 5 levels, cited per cut) and one half-axis (`tgt` labelled 'יעד מרקם' vs `safe`). We even TELL the user 'time affects texture only' (app.js:3049) and then compute nothing from it. The chewiness prediction is the most product-differentiating item in the whole proposal: `methodRules` already encodes the physics (`needsCookFor:'grill'`, `invalid:[['grill']]` for collagen cuts) — it just refuses silently instead of explaining what would have gone wrong.

conceptsFound.concept: Conditional stage boundaries — a stage ends on TIME or on INTERNAL TEMPERATURE, whichever comes first (`TRIGGER_NEXT_STAGE_WHEN`)
conceptsFound.steelman: Real cooks do not run a clock; they run a probe. A stage carries a duration ESTIMATE for planning and a TRIGGER for execution. The estimate feeds the schedule; the trigger feeds the instruction, the alarm, and later the re-plan. Adding a trigger field changes no arithmetic — it changes what the app can say and what it can react to.
conceptsFound.value: `planSchedule` (app.js:3859) chains fixed `hours` backward from serve; there is no representation for a conditional boundary anywhere. The stall wrap is cited data (`mid:'עטיפה ב-70°C'`, `somid:'עטיפה ב-75°C'` on ~40 cuts) trapped in a prose string. Consequence chain: the wrap never becomes a stage → never becomes an EQM requires row (so butcher paper/foil are never 'missing equipment') → never becomes a timeline task → never reaches the AI grounding. This is a correctness gap, not a feature gap.

conceptsFound.concept: A declarative hard-rule set with typed action classes (block / adjust / warn / append-stage / force-action)
conceptsFound.steelman: Rules become data: ordered, enumerable, individually citable, individually testable, and inspectable at runtime ('which rule blocked me, and on what authority'). New rules are added without touching call sites; every consumer reads one uniform verdict object.
conceptsFound.value: We HAVE the rules — `methodRules`+`validCombo`, `grillable:False` in `CUT_SOURCES`, `eqmDeviceMeetsRow`'s capability gates, `deviceCanReach`'s temp ceiling, `schedulePlacements`' six conflict reasons, Phase-3a's `safetyGate` and `holdCapMin`. They are imperative, scattered across five files, and only ONE family (equipment) produces a machine-readable verdict. `eqmValidity` returning `{level, okPaths, gaps, fixes}` is already a beautiful rule-engine output — it just has exactly one rule family behind it. Generalizing that shape is mostly harvesting work we already did.

conceptsFound.concept: Glaze/sauce as a computed rule (sugar content × chamber temp × time remaining → DELAY_GLAZE), and split application (salt in the bag, glaze on the finish)
conceptsFound.steelman: Glaze timing is a function, not a constant: sugar burns above a threshold chamber temperature, so the glaze window is derived from the finish stage's cited temp; and if the finish is wet/vacuum there is no glaze window at all, so the rule must reroute or refuse.
conceptsFound.value: Today glaze is unconditional: app.js:7273 schedules 'brush glaze' at `lastCook.end − 15min` for any selected glaze on any path, and app.js:1288 prints 'last 10-15 minutes' as prose. A sugar glaze on the 230°C shrimp path and on a 68°C sous-vide-only path get the identical instruction. We already carry everything the rule needs — `SEASONINGS[].kind==='glaze'`, `SEASONING_TAGS[].flavor` includes 'מתוק', and every stage carries `temp` — so this is a cheap, visible win.

conceptsFound.concept: Flavor layer as a plugin that never changes physics, with a protein↔profile compatibility matrix and combination rules (no oil in the SV bag; no sugar under prolonged high smoke)
conceptsFound.steelman: Seasoning is orthogonal to heat management and should be modelled as an overlay with its own compatibility and application-timing rules, so the physics engine stays small and the flavor library grows independently.
conceptsFound.value: We are ahead here: 354 seasonings with `kind`/`cont`/`cats`, plus `SEASONING_TAGS` giving `flavor[]`/`base`/`heat` per item, plus per-cut `rub`/`wood`/`coal`. Their §7 is a three-row table. What we lack is only the small set of APPLICATION rules (§4.2) — which the rule registry gives us for free once it exists.

conceptsFound.concept: Method conversion engine — source→target method with a time factor plus explicit LOSS_OF_ATTR / GAIN_OF_ATTR
conceptsFound.steelman: When a user swaps method, tell them the honest trade in the same breath as the new time: 'faster, but you lose bark and smoke aroma'. The attribute delta is the valuable half; the multiplier is the disposable half.
conceptsFound.value: The multiplier is exactly what we must NOT take — a formula-derived cook time is a safety-number invention and violates the cited-only rule. But the ATTRIBUTE DELTA is pure prose-free metadata and is precisely what an outcome layer needs to explain a ranking: our `order_svsmoke`/`order_smokesv` pairs and the `sot/soh` (smoke-only) column already ARE cited method conversions — we just never say what each one costs you. `svSmokeFinish` computes 'חוסך מעשנת' (saved smoker-hours) and stops there.

conceptsFound.concept: Equipment-driven feasibility with structured reasons and remedies (§4.3, simulation B: 'cheddar needs cold smoke <30°C; your oven and grill cannot; buy a cold-smoke coil')
conceptsFound.steelman: A refusal is only useful if it names the constraint, the failing device property, and the cheapest fix.
conceptsFound.value: E1/E2/E3 already ship this and ship it better: `eqmValidity` → `{level:'ok'|'blocked-default'|'uncookable', okPaths, gaps:[{kind,state}], fixes:[configure|switch-path|replace-e5]}`, evaluated against ALL cited paths, with a generation-stamped cache, retroactive-delete warning, and two distinct event-window reasons ('missing X' vs 'busy in this window: X'). Their version throws a string.

conceptsFound.concept: Device class → smoke-intensity coefficient (offset 1.5 … electric 0.6) as a first-class device attribute
conceptsFound.steelman: Not all smokers deliver the same smoke for the same wood and time; a coefficient lets the engine adjust *guidance* (use a smoke tube, run max-smoke early) rather than adjust temperatures.
conceptsFound.value: We have the knowledge as prose tips keyed by device type (app.js:1092: 'פלט: … הוסף צינור/מבוך עשן … max smoke בשעתיים הראשונות'), not as a number a rule can compare. As a NON-safety, advisory-only coefficient it is safe to adopt — but it must be quarantined from anything that touches time or temperature, and it must be sourced, not invented.

conceptsFound.concept: Spatial + temporal co-optimization: shelf allocation and backward scheduling in one pass
conceptsFound.steelman: Place and schedule together, because freeing a shelf is a scheduling move and staggering is a placement move.
conceptsFound.value: `schedulePlacements` already does latest-first placement with a bounded earlier-pull (`SCHED_PULL_MAX_MS`), per-slot fit, hanging-as-hooks, bath sharing by temperature, and six typed conflict reasons. Their `optimizeEvent` decrements `shelf_area_cm2` on the device object in a loop with no packing efficiency, no measurement confidence, no hanging, and no time dimension in the spatial pass at all.

conceptsFound.concept: Fleet management: several devices, load-balancing an item to a secondary cooker when the primary overflows
conceptsFound.steelman: Treat the kit as a fleet with a substitution ladder, so 'no room' becomes 'no room anywhere' only after every device was tried.
conceptsFound.value: `cookerCandidates(kind)` already implements the substitution policy (smoke→smoker|charcoal/kettle/gas grill; cook→grill|oven; sv→bath) and `EQM.availability` already walks candidates until one fits. What is missing is the ORCHESTRATOR-level reassign across a whole menu — which is exactly Phase-3a's `reassign` rung, already specced and approved. So: adopt nothing new, just finish P8.

conceptsFound.concept: Insulated cooler (Faux Cambro) as an explicit scheduling BUFFER that both holds food and frees rack space
conceptsFound.steelman: A held item is a scheduling resource: it decouples finish time from serve time and returns capacity to the device. Modelling the hold as a first-class move makes 'cook early' safe to propose.
conceptsFound.value: Phase-3a already has `cook-early-and-hold` with a hold floor of 60°C, a 240-min danger-zone accumulator, a per-category ban (never poultry/fish/lean/medium-rare) and a 360-min hard cap. Ours is strictly safer — theirs would cheerfully hold chicken for four hours. The one genuinely new idea worth taking is the CAPACITY effect: holding an item should RELEASE its EQM ledger entry, which our ledger can express today (`EQM.release`) and our solver does not yet use.

conceptsFound.concept: Telemetry loop: observed internal temp → predicted ETA vs serve time → stall detection → crisis re-plan; plus device-failure recovery ladder
conceptsFound.steelman: The plan is a hypothesis. Feed it one observation (the probe reading, however it arrives — even typed by hand) and it becomes a live controller: predict the finish, compare to serve, and if it will miss, name the cited intervention (wrap, raise chamber, move to oven, hold in cooler).
conceptsFound.value: We have zero 'now' input. `schedulePlacements` runs once at render and the plan never learns. The parts already exist — windows, ledger, placement, conflict reasons, a hold rung — and the missing piece is one observation store plus a re-entry point. Deliberately, our version should default to MANUAL entry, which sidesteps their entire §6.1 vendor-cloud problem and keeps the app offline-capable.

conceptsFound.concept: Consumables calculator with a per-line JUSTIFICATION ('9 kg charcoal — 0.8 kg/h × 9 h + 20% for wind')
conceptsFound.steelman: A shopping list that explains its own arithmetic is auditable and teaches; a bare number is a guess the user cannot check.
conceptsFound.value: We have refuel CADENCE as a device fact (`REFUEL_MIN`, with an explicit 'unknown device gets 0 rather than an invented cadence' rule) and a shopping list, but no fuel QUANTITY. The consumption rates would need sourcing like everything else; the reusable idea is the reason-string pattern, which fits our existing citation UI directly.

conceptsFound.concept: Structured refusal with cause + remedy as the standard output shape for every engine decision, not just equipment
conceptsFound.steelman: Every 'no' the engine emits carries: what was requested, which rule fired, what data authorises that rule, and the ordered list of cheapest fixes. One component renders all of them.
conceptsFound.value: `eqmValidity`+`eqInvPanelHtml` do this for equipment. Everything else degrades: `schedulePlacements` conflicts render through `_schedAdviceHtml` as hand-built sentences, and — worth flagging — those calls build strings like `L('לא נכנס יחד עם השאר ל'+dev+' …', …)`, i.e. COMPUTED arguments to `L()`, which the acorn extractor cannot see. That is a live i18n hole (Guard A can only enforce keys it knows about), and unifying the verdict shape closes it as a side effect.

whereItBeatsUs:
Five places, plainly.

**1. Stage boundaries are unconditional in our engine, and that hides cited data.** `planSchedule` (app.js:3859) walks stages backward from serve using `Number(s.hours)` only. `itemStages` (app.js:4093) emits no wrap stage, ever. Meanwhile `data.py` carries `mid="עטיפה ב-70°C"` / `somid="עטיפה ב-75°C"` on roughly 40 collagen cuts — a real, cited, numeric trigger — which is rendered as decorative prose at app.js:1562/1586 and read by nothing else. Their `TRIGGER_NEXT_STAGE_WHEN = (TIME_ELAPSED == 2h) OR (P_TARGET_INT == 50°C)` is a strictly better stage model. Because the wrap is not a stage, `deriveRequires` (equipment.js:63) never emits a requires row for butcher paper or foil — so E3 will call a brisket cook "ok" for a user who owns neither, and the timeline never tells anyone to wrap.

**2. Nothing routes from outcome to path.** `itemPaths` (app.js:4175) labels paths by mechanism (`'⚡ סו-ויד + עישון (מהכרטיסייה)'`) and `eqmValidity`'s `switch-path` fix repeats that label. `gearAwareDefault` (app.js:1027) routes by equipment and does it well, but there is no function anywhere that takes a desired result and returns a path. Their §8 four-step flow ("מהיר" / "פריכה ומסורתית" / "נימוחה ועסיסית") is the better product, and it costs us nothing in safety because the routing selects among paths we already cite.

**3. Glaze is a constant, not a rule.** app.js:7273 places the glaze task at `lastCook.end − 15min` for every selected glaze on every path, unconditionally; app.js:1288 hardcodes "last 10-15 minutes". No check on whether the last stage is dry heat, no check of `s.temp` against a sugar-burn threshold, no gate when the path ends in a vacuum or a bath. Their §4.2 rule is correct and we have all the inputs (`SEASONINGS[].kind`, `SEASONING_TAGS[].flavor` containing 'מתוק', `stage.temp`) sitting unused.

**4. No chewiness/texture prediction.** `methodRules` (app.js:989) encodes exactly the physics their Rule 1 encodes — `needsCookFor:'grill'`, `invalid:[['grill']]` for collagen cuts — but expresses it only as *absence*: `validCombo` returns false, the combo silently disappears from `itemProfile`'s enumeration, and the user is never told the path exists and would produce shoe leather. Same for `grillable:False` in `CUT_SOURCES`, which carries a full Hebrew explanation ("אש ישירה חזקה תחרוך את החוץ בעוד הפנים נשאר קשה") that no code path surfaces as a *reason*.

**5. The plan never learns.** `schedulePlacements` is one-shot at render; there is no store, function or field anywhere that accepts "the brisket is at 71° and has been for 90 minutes". Their §5.5 `processTelemetry` / `handleDeviceFailure` loop is a different class of system, and our building blocks (windows, `EQM` ledger, `cookerCandidates`, Phase-3a hold rung) are all present and idle.

Minor but real: no fuel-quantity math (we have `REFUEL_MIN` cadence only), and no smoke-intensity coefficient per smoker class (we have it as prose tips at app.js:1092).
whereWeAreBetter:
**Citation architecture.** `sources.py` merges 279 citations at build; `CUT_SOURCES[n]` carries per-facet refs (`sv`/`smoke`/`safe`/`grill`), `grillable:False` as a cited hard flag, and — the part that has no analogue in the proposal — **per-ORDER cited schedules**: `order_svsmoke` and `order_smokesv` each with their own `{t,h,cold}` and their own reference. `itemStages` reads them and falls back to a conservative computed value only when data is absent, with the fallback explicitly marked in the label. The proposal has one hardcoded pipeline and a note that real numbers come from USDA.

**Occupancy modelling.** `deviceCapacity` + `eqDeriveAreaCm2` + `eqDeviceSuspect` + `PACK_EFF` (0.85) + a per-slot floor whose tolerance branches on `areaMeasured` (`FIT_SLOT_TOL` 1.10 measured vs `FIT_HARD_FACTOR` 1.6 estimated). We track the *provenance* of every area number and refuse to grant an estimate the confidence of a measurement. Their §5.2 decrements `equipment.shelf_area_cm2` on the device object in a placement loop — no packing efficiency, no hanging, no measurement confidence, and the mutation makes the function non-reentrant.

**The negative case is engineered, not incidental.** `eqmFitVerdict` returns `fits:false` when `!cap.known` — an unmeasured device NEVER silently absorbs a booking. `eqmDeviceMeetsRow` gates capability (temp reach, bath volume, hang, standalone probe) *before* capacity is even considered, precisely so a right-kind wrong-capability device cannot be reported free. `EQM.availability`'s D11 case makes "✓ everything fits" structurally unreachable on an empty registry. Their `allocateFleetAndSpace` places into any device whose number is large enough, including one whose size was never entered.

**Hold safety.** Phase-3a's floors are strictly stronger: 60°C hold floor, 240-min cumulative danger-zone accumulator per item, category ban (never poultry, fish, lean, or anything served medium-rare), `holdCapMin` 360 min as an absolute gate *plus* a separate lower solver-generation ceiling. Their `TRANSFER_TO_COOLER` fires on `timeUntilServing > required_resting_mins` for any item at all.

**Sous-vide is modelled as a shared resource with temperature exclusivity** in both directions — the intra-event detector (`schedulePlacements` `bath-temp` conflict) and the cross-event ledger (`eqmFitVerdict`'s volume branch comparing `demand.tempC` across held entries, with a deliberate no-epsilon exact comparison). Theirs is a vessel with a litre count.

**`safetyDiff` (app.js:3919)** — a runtime invariant that compares a transformed plan against its own pre-transform self on kind/hours/temp/safe, so a future edit to a placer or repair rung cannot silently shorten a cook. The proposal's engine freely does `SET P_TARGET_INT = 52` with nothing watching.

**The i18n machine.** Guard A (every known key translated in every active language, identical-to-source rejected), Guard B (unit-class-preserving numeric safety across 23 scripts — a g↔kg or °C↔°F swap fails the build), Guard C (translator garbage). Any engine that emits prose would tear this down; ours cannot, because the engine will emit codes.
proposedModel:
## Target architecture — seven layers, three of them new

The organising principle: **rules feed `itemStages`; they never bypass it.** `itemStages` remains the single stage authority for every surface (card, catalog row, work plan, EQM, AI grounding). Everything new either produces input to it or consumes its output.

### L0 · CITED (build-time data) — extended, discipline unchanged
New `thresholds.py`, same rules as `sources.py`:
```python
THRESHOLDS = {
  'stall.wrap_c':       {'v': 71, 'ref': 'AmazingRibs — The Stall', 'url': '…'},
  'glaze.max_chamber_c':{'v': 140, 'ref': '…', 'url': '…'},
  'coldsmoke.max_c':    {'v': 30,  'ref': '…', 'url': '…'},
  'hold.floor_c':       {'v': 60,  'ref': 'FSIS hot-holding', 'url': '…'},
  'dangerzone.budget_min': {'v': 240, 'ref': 'FSIS 2-hour/4-hour', 'url': '…'},
}
```
This harvests numbers that today are bare literals in `app.js` (`TEMP_TOL_C=6`, the 60/240/360 in the Phase-3a spec, the `<30°C` cheese rule that lives only in help text) and puts them under the citation regime they should always have had. Merged at build exactly like `CUT_SOURCES`.

New `item_facts.py`, **derived not hand-typed**, in the proven `equipment_map.py` idiom:
```python
# facts = {'collagen':'high'|'low', 'lean': bool, 'skin': bool, 'served_rare': bool,
#          'shape':'slab|roast|pieces|bird|long', 'thickness_class':'thin|med|thick',
#          'protein':'beef|poultry|pork|lamb|fish|shellfish|offal|produce|dairy'}
```
Derived from `cat` / `doneness` / `tgt` vs `safe` / `kg` / existing `equip.spec.shape`. Today `isProduce`, `isOffal` and `c.doneness` each re-derive a piece of this inline in three different functions.

### L1 · RULES (new module `rules.js`, inlined before `app.js` like `equipment.js`)
```js
// A rule is DATA. Ordered. Pure. Emits typed codes only — never prose, never a number it authored.
// RULE = { id, phase, when, action, code, params, cite, severity }
//   phase   'path' | 'stage' | 'plan' | 'live'      — when in the pipeline it runs
//   when    (ctx) => boolean                        — pure predicate over the typed ctx
//   action  'block' | 'warn' | 'adjust' | 'append-stage' | 'insert-stage' | 'require'
//   code    stable SCREAMING_SNAKE enum             — the ONLY thing the render layer switches on
//   params  (ctx) => ({...numbers/enums from ctx.cited ONLY})
//   cite    (ctx) => {ref,url} | null               — the authority for this rule firing
const RULES = [
  { id:'R-COLLAGEN-DIRECT-GRILL', phase:'path', severity:'block',
    when: c => c.facts.collagen==='high' && c.path.combo.length===1 && c.path.combo[0]==='grill',
    action:'block', code:'BLOCK_COLLAGEN_NEEDS_LONG_COOK',
    params: c => ({ targetC: c.cited.tgt }),
    cite:  c => c.cited.src.grill },

  { id:'R-STALL-WRAP', phase:'stage', severity:'info',
    when: c => c.facts.collagen==='high' && c.stage.kind==='smoke' && c.cited.wrapC!=null,
    action:'insert-stage', code:'STAGE_WRAP_AT_STALL',
    params: c => ({ triggerTempC: c.cited.wrapC, material:'butcher_paper|foil' }),
    cite:  c => c.cited.src.smoke },

  { id:'R-GLAZE-WINDOW', phase:'stage', severity:'warn',
    when: c => c.flavor.hasSugarGlaze && c.stage.isLastCook && c.stage.temp > c.thr('glaze.max_chamber_c'),
    action:'append-stage', code:'STAGE_GLAZE_LATE_ONLY',
    params: c => ({ windowMin: 15, chamberC: c.stage.temp }),
    cite:  c => c.thrCite('glaze.max_chamber_c') },

  { id:'R-GLAZE-NO-DRY-FINISH', phase:'path', severity:'warn',
    when: c => c.flavor.hasSugarGlaze && !c.path.hasDryHeatFinish,
    action:'warn', code:'WARN_GLAZE_NEEDS_DRY_FINISH', params: ()=>({}), cite: ()=>null },

  { id:'R-CHEW-RISK', phase:'path', severity:'warn',
    when: c => c.facts.collagen==='high' && c.path.collagenDwellHrs < c.cited.minDwellHrs,
    action:'warn', code:'WARN_WILL_BE_CHEWY',
    params: c => ({ haveHrs: c.path.collagenDwellHrs, needHrs: c.cited.minDwellHrs }),
    cite:  c => c.cited.src.sv },
];
```
**Evaluation:**
```js
function evaluate(ctx)  // → { blocks:[V], warns:[V], stages:[StageOp], requires:[Row] }
// V = { code, params, cite, ruleId, severity }
```
`ctx` is a frozen typed record — `{facts, cited, path, stage, flavor, equipKit, thr, thrCite}`. It contains no DOM, no `store`, no `localStorage`. That purity is what makes a golden-corpus equivalence test possible.

**The i18n seam (constraint b), stated precisely.** A separate `RULE_COPY` object in `app.js` — a *literal* map of static `L()` calls, one per code:
```js
const RULE_COPY = {
  BLOCK_COLLAGEN_NEEDS_LONG_COOK: (p) =>
    L('נתח עתיר קולגן — אש ישירה תחרוך את החוץ והפנים יישאר קשה. דרוש בישול ארוך.',
      'A high-collagen cut — direct fire chars the outside while the inside stays tough. Needs a long cook.'),
  STAGE_WRAP_AT_STALL: (p) =>
    L('עטוף בהגעה לטמפ׳ הפנים','Wrap when the internal temp reaches'),
  WARN_WILL_BE_CHEWY: (p) =>
    L('בזמן הזה הנתח ייצא לעיס — הקולגן לא הספיק להתפרק.',
      'At this duration the cut will come out chewy — the collagen has not broken down.'),
};
```
Numbers are rendered by the CALLER as `dir="ltr"` islands from `p.*`, never interpolated into the `L()` argument. Two new build guards enforce this:
- **Guard E (exhaustiveness):** every `code` string appearing in `rules.js` has a `RULE_COPY` entry; every `RULE_COPY` key is a live code. Fails the build otherwise — the same shape as Guard A.
- **Guard F (no authored numbers):** an acorn pass over `rules.js` rejects any numeric literal outside `0`, `1`, array indices and a small explicitly-cited allow-list. Every threshold must come through `c.thr('key')`. This is the mechanical enforcement of "cited values remain the only source of safety numbers", and it is cheap because we already run acorn over the source for the L() extractor.

### L2 · OUTCOME (new, `outcome.js` or a section of `rules.js`)
```js
const OUTCOME_AXES = {
  finish:  { values:['juicy-uniform','shreddable','firm-sliceable'], def:null },
  crust:   { values:['none','soft-bark','hard-bark','crisp-skin'],  def:null },
  smoke:   { values:['none','light','deep'],                         def:null },
  speed:   { values:['fast','standard','overnight'],                 def:'standard' },
};
// PURE SELECTOR — filters and ranks itemPaths(meta). Never emits a number.
function routePaths(meta, outcome){
  // → [{ pathId, score, matched:['finish','crust'], tradeoffs:[{code,params}], blocked:[V] }]
}
function pathOutcomes(meta, path){ /* → {finish, crust, smoke, speed} derived from CITED path data */ }
```
`pathOutcomes` reads only cited facts already in the data: sv-first ⇒ `finish:'juicy-uniform'`; `order_smokesv` with `cold:true` ⇒ `smoke:'deep'`; a smoke stage above a bark threshold ⇒ `crust:'hard-bark'`; total hours ⇒ `speed`. **The chew warning is an output of `routePaths`, not an input axis** — the user never asks for chewy; the engine predicts it.

### L3 · PLAN — `itemStages` extended, not replaced
Two additive changes, both zero-arithmetic:
1. Stages gain an optional `until:{tempC}` alongside `hours`. `hours` stays the scheduling estimate (`planSchedule` untouched); `until` is what the card, timeline and probe surface display, and what L5 later consumes.
2. `itemStages` runs `evaluate(ctx).stages` as a **post-pass** that may `insert-stage`/`append-stage` — producing real `kind:'wrap'` / `kind:'glaze'` / `kind:'score-skin'` stages. `deriveRequires` (equipment.js) picks up new `REQ_KIND` entries automatically, so butcher paper and foil become genuine EQM requires rows with no change to E1/E2/E3.

### L4 · VERDICT — one shape for all rule families
Promote `eqmValidity`'s return shape into the universal one:
```js
function itemVerdict(meta, pathSel)   // → { level:'ok'|'blocked-default'|'uncookable',
                                      //     okPaths, blocks:[V], warns:[V], fixes:[Fix] }
```
`eqmValidity` becomes the equipment-family *contributor* to it (its `gaps`→`blocks`, its `fixes` merged). `eqInvPanelHtml` becomes `verdictPanelHtml` and renders codes through `RULE_COPY` — which also retires the computed-argument `L()` calls in `_schedAdviceHtml` (app.js ~4076), an existing extractor blind spot.

### L5 · TELEMETRY seam (last wave)
```js
function observe(scope, {itemKey, internalC, atMs, source:'manual'|'probe'})  // → void, writes mk-obs-<scope>
function predictFinish(itemKey, scope)     // → { etaMs, confidence:'low'|'med', basis:'rate'|'cited' }
function replan(scope)                     // → orchestrate() over the SAME solver, with observations folded in
```
Manual entry is the default and only shipped input — no vendor cloud, offline intact. `predictFinish` is advisory-only and its output is never written back into any stage's `hours` or `temp` (`safetyDiff` proves it). Stall detection = `internalC` inside a cited stall band with a flat rate over N minutes → a `WARN_STALL_WILL_MISS_SERVE` code whose remedy list comes from RULES, ranked by the Phase-3a solver.

### Waves — each independently shippable, app releasable after every one

**Wave 0 · Foundations (invisible).** `thresholds.py` with citations, `item_facts.py` derivation, Guard F skeleton. No UI, no behaviour change. **~3 tasks ≈ 0.3 CP2.**

**Wave 1 · Rule registry, behaviour-preserving.** `rules.js` + `evaluate` + `RULE_COPY` + Guards E/F. Port `methodRules`/`validCombo`/`deviceCanReach` into RULES behind adapters. **Ships zero new behaviour** and is proven by the golden corpus (below). **~5 tasks ≈ 0.8 CP2.**

**Wave 2 · Structured modifier stages.** Extract wrap trigger / glaze window / skin treatment from `mid`/`somid` into cited structured fields (Python, derived); rules emit them as real stages with `until`; EQM gains paper/foil requires rows for free; the glaze rule replaces the unconditional −15 min. UI-visible ⇒ mockup + owner approval per §10.9. **~6 tasks ≈ 1.0 CP2.**

**Wave 3 · Outcome layer + CP2.** `OUTCOME_AXES`, `pathOutcomes`, `routePaths`, chew prediction; the card panel becomes outcome-first with the mechanism name as subtitle. **This is the wave that changes CP2** — see below. **~7 tasks ≈ 1.2 CP2 gross, ≈ 0.5 net over the existing CP2 plan.**

**Wave 4 · Unified verdict.** `itemVerdict` + `verdictPanelHtml`; `eqmValidity` folded in; `_schedAdviceHtml` retired (closing its extractor blind spot). **~4 tasks ≈ 0.6 CP2.**

**Wave 5 · Telemetry / re-plan.** `observe`/`predictFinish`/`replan`, manual entry, stall warning, device-failure reassign via `cookerCandidates` + ledger. Depends on Phase-3a (P8) landing first. **~6 tasks ≈ 1.0 CP2.**

**Wave 6 (optional, gated on evidence) · Archetype compression.** Derive `PROCESS_ARCHETYPES` from the 279 recipes after Waves 1–3 make the structure explicit; keep per-recipe cited deltas. Do not start speculatively — start only if Wave 2's derivation shows the clustering is real. **~6 tasks ≈ 1.0 CP2.**

**Total through Wave 5: ≈ 4.4 CP2-equivalents ≈ 31 tasks / ~430 code blocks.** With Wave 6: ≈ 5.4.

### How CP2 changes, and the Waiver Gate
The approved CP2 plan (11 tasks, 150 blocks) builds an expandable list of paths labelled by mechanism, with a per-recipe default in `mk-item-path`. Wave 3 keeps **all of its infrastructure** — `MK_ITEM_PATH`, `setItemPath`, `itemDefaultPath`, `pathCited`, the placeholder rows, the byte-identical-when-nothing-stored invariant — and changes only the **top of the panel**: outcome chips above the list, the list ranked by `routePaths`, each row annotated with its predicted outcome and any chew/crust trade-off, and the CP3 placeholders unchanged. Tasks 1–2 and 8–11 of the CP2 plan survive verbatim; Tasks 3–7 (the panel render + selection wiring) are rewritten.

**This is a spec change and must go to the owner in conversation before any code (§4).** Two options to put to him: (a) ship CP2 exactly as approved now and add the outcome layer as Wave 3 on top (lower risk, two panel revisions, two rounds of screenshots and translations); or (b) amend the CP2 spec before building, so the panel is built outcome-first once. My recommendation is **(b)** — the panel is the product surface for this entire idea, and building it twice costs more than amending the spec once.

### Biggest technical risk, and how I de-risk it
**Silent behavioural drift during the Wave-1 port.** The rule set will end up subtly different from the imperative code it replaces, across 279 recipes × up to 7 valid combos × 2 orders × an equipment-kit matrix — a space no human reviews and no existing test covers exhaustively. Our DoD catches a failing assertion, not a plausible-but-different one; the 816-test suite would stay green while brisket quietly lost a path.

**Mitigation — a golden-corpus equivalence harness, built BEFORE Wave 1 and committed:** one Playwright `page.evaluate` over the real shipped build snapshots, for every item and every path, the full output of `itemStages`, `validCombo`, `itemPaths`, `deriveRequires` and `eqmValidity` under a fixed matrix of seeded equipment kits, into `tests/_golden/engine-corpus.json`. Wave 1's acceptance criterion is **byte-identical reproduction**; any intended change must appear as an explicit reviewed diff line in that fixture, with the rule id that caused it named in the commit. Waves 2–5 then regenerate the corpus deliberately, so every subsequent behavioural change is visible as data rather than inferred from prose. This is roughly one task to build and it is the only thing that makes a refactor of this size safe under our own discipline.

Second-order risk: **the extractor cannot see rule copy if it is written cleverly.** Mitigated structurally by Guard E (exhaustive literal `RULE_COPY`) plus the standing rule that numbers are rendered by the caller as `dir="ltr"` islands from `params`, never interpolated into an `L()` argument — which is the same lesson L13 and v274–v277 already paid for.
openQuestions: **CP2 sequencing — owner decision required (Waiver Gate §4).** Amend the approved CP2 spec now so the path panel is built outcome-first once, or ship CP2 as approved and revise the panel in Wave 3? Two panel revisions means two mockups, two screenshot rounds and two sets of six-language strings.

**Where do the new thresholds get their citations?** `glaze.max_chamber_c`, `coldsmoke.max_c`, a minimum collagen-dwell duration per cut class, and a bark-formation threshold are all currently either absent or living as uncited prose in help text (app.js:4753-4789). They are non-safety in the FSIS sense but they gate user-facing claims. Do they go through the same `sources.py` regime, or do we create a second, clearly-labelled advisory tier?

**Is chewiness derivable from data we hold, or does it need new cited research?** The prediction needs a minimum collagen-dwell duration per cut class. We have `svh`/`smh`/`soh` (what the cited path does) but no cited statement of the minimum below which the result is chewy. Without that number the warning can only fire on the trivial case (`validCombo` already false), which is much less valuable.

**Manual-only telemetry, or a probe adapter?** Manual entry keeps the app offline-capable and dodges the vendor-cloud problem entirely, but a stall alert nobody is awake to type into is worth little. Is a MEATER/Inkbird adapter (which needs the Worker and a scheduled poll) in scope at all, or is Wave 5 explicitly a manual-observation feature?

**Does an item held in a cooler release its EQM ledger entry?** Their Faux Cambro insight is that holding frees rack capacity. Our ledger can express it (`EQM.release`), but doing so means an item can be 'in the plan' while holding no equipment — a new state that `deviceOccupancy` and `cookerContention` have never seen. Worth confirming this is the intended semantics before Wave 5 depends on it.

**How far does archetype compression go before it stops being safe?** Compressing structure is safe; compressing cited scalars into an archetype default is not. Where exactly is the line — may an archetype supply a *rest duration* or a *dry-surface duration*, which are non-safety, or must every scalar stay per-recipe and cited?

**Should `RULE_COPY` live in `app.js` or in a fourth inlined file?** `rules.js` must stay prose-free for Guard F to be simple, but keeping the copy in `app.js` puts a growing static map in an already ~11.5k-line file. A separate `rules-copy.js` inlined between them keeps both guards trivial at the cost of a fourth build input.
